alignment.note: The Vulgate entirely omits Mark 9:49, which appears in both Greek and Peshitta traditions. This verse ('Everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt') is textually complex in Greek manuscripts, with significant Western witnesses (D, some Old Latin) lacking it or presenting variant forms. The Clementine Vulgate's omission reflects this Western textual tradition, proceeding directly from 9:48 to 9:50.

The Vulgate substitutes the entire content of Mark 9:49 with material from 9:50 ('Salt is good; but if the salt becomes tasteless, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another'). This represents a conflation or displacement where the Vulgate tradition has relocated verse 50's content to the position of verse 49, creating a major textual divergence from both Greek and Syriac witnesses.
